label: Short A
articulation: Low front vowel. Open your mouth wide, spread your lips slightly, and keep the tongue low and pushed forward.
learnerTip: Think of the sound a surprised person makes — short, open, forward. Longer than /ɛ/, wider than /ɑ/.
commonErrors: Raised too high, sounding like /ɛ/ (especially before nasals)
Replaced with /ɑː/ by Spanish or Portuguese speakers
Pin-pen merger: sounds like /ɪ/ before nasals in Southern American English
viNote: Tiếng Việt không có âm này; người Việt hay đọc thành "e" hoặc "a". Mở miệng rộng như "a" nhưng đẩy lưỡi ra trước như "e": cat, man, bad.

label: Short E
articulation: Mid front vowel. Mouth half-open, lips slightly spread, tongue mid-height and forward.
learnerTip: Relax your jaw halfway between /iː/ and /æ/. Think of 'eh?' — a questioning sound.
commonErrors: Confused with /æ/ — /ɛ/ is higher and less open
Confused with /eɪ/ — keep it short and pure, no glide
Replaced with /e/ (tenser version) by European speakers
viNote: Gần với "e" trong "mẹ". Giữ âm ngắn, không lướt thành "ây": bed khác bayed.

label: Short I
articulation: High front lax vowel. Tongue near the top of the mouth but relaxed, slightly lower than /iː/. Lips spread but loose.
learnerTip: Say /iː/ then relax and lower your tongue slightly. The sound is shorter and less tense.
commonErrors: Replaced with /iː/ — keep it short and lax, not tense
Confused with /ɛ/ by French or Spanish speakers
Merged with /iː/ in some dialects (e.g. feel/fill)
viNote: Ngắn và lỏng hơn "i" tiếng Việt. Đừng kéo dài thành /iː/, nếu không ship sẽ nghe như sheep.

label: Short O (RP)
articulation: Open back rounded vowel (RP). Mouth open, tongue low and back, lips loosely rounded.
learnerTip: In GA this vowel merges with /ɑː/ (the lot-palm merger). In RP it is short and rounded. Think of a British 'pot'.
commonErrors: GA speakers may not distinguish this from /ɑː/
Over-rounded by learners aiming for RP
dialectNote: In General American, /ɒ/ and /ɑː/ are merged. This phoneme is primarily an RP distinction.
viNote: Gần "o" trong "có" nhưng ngắn hơn. Giọng Mỹ thường mở rộng thành /ɑ/: hot, stop.

label: Short U
articulation: Open-mid central to back vowel. Mouth half-open, tongue central, no lip rounding.
learnerTip: Relax everything. Neutral, unstressed sound in the middle of the mouth. Like a short grunt.
commonErrors: Confused with /ʊ/ — /ʌ/ has no lip rounding
Replaced with /ɑː/ or /a/ by European speakers
Not distinguished from /ʊ/ in some dialects (foot-strut merger)
viNote: Gần "â" hoặc "ơ" ngắn (cup gần "cấp"). Môi thả lỏng, không tròn môi.

label: Short OO
articulation: High back lax rounded vowel. Tongue high and back, lips loosely rounded. Less tense than /uː/.
learnerTip: Like /uː/ but shorter and with less lip rounding. Say 'oo' then relax your lips and tongue.
commonErrors: Replaced with /uː/ — keep it short and lax
Confused with /ʌ/ — /ʊ/ has lip rounding
Not distinguished from /uː/ in some dialects (pool-pull merger)
viNote: Gần "u" nhưng ngắn và lỏng hơn, môi tròn nhẹ. Đừng kéo dài: full khác fool.

label: Schwa
articulation: Mid central neutral vowel. Fully relaxed mouth, tongue in the center, no lip rounding. The most common English sound.
learnerTip: The schwa only appears in unstressed syllables. Never stress a schwa — it should be quick and throwaway.
commonErrors: Over-pronouncing it as a full vowel (common in speakers whose L1 lacks schwa reduction)
Spelling-based pronunciation: saying 'sup-PORT' with a clear /o/ instead of schwa
Missing it in consonant clusters
viNote: Âm yếu nhất tiếng Anh, gần "ơ" rất nhẹ và ngắn. Người Việt hay đọc rõ mọi âm tiết; hãy đọc lướt âm tiết không nhấn: about, banana.

label: Long E
articulation: Close front tense vowel. Tongue high and forward, lips spread into a smile position. Hold it longer than /ɪ/.
learnerTip: Spread your lips like a big smile and hold the sound. Your tongue should feel near the roof of your mouth.
commonErrors: Shortened to /ɪ/ — hold the length and tension
Not distinguished from /ɪ/ in some dialects
viNote: Giống "i" tiếng Việt nhưng kéo dài, môi hơi bè. Phân biệt độ dài: sheep /iː/ khác ship /ɪ/.

label: Long OO
articulation: Close back tense rounded vowel. Tongue high and back, lips strongly rounded and protruded.
learnerTip: Round your lips into a tight circle as if kissing. The sound is long and tense.
commonErrors: Shortened to /ʊ/ — hold the length and rounding
Under-rounded by speakers whose L1 lacks rounded vowels
viNote: Giống "u" tiếng Việt nhưng dài hơn, môi tròn. food /uː/ khác foot /ʊ/.

label: Long AH
articulation: Open back unrounded vowel. Mouth wide open, tongue low and back, no lip rounding. Like saying 'ah' at the doctor.
learnerTip: Drop your jaw completely and say 'ah'. Keep it long and open, no movement of tongue or lips.
commonErrors: Shortened by non-rhotic speakers adding /r/ where none exists
Confused with /æ/ — /ɑː/ is further back and longer
viNote: Giống "a" tiếng Việt nhưng sâu và dài hơn, miệng mở rộng: father, car.

label: AW Sound
articulation: Open-mid back rounded vowel. Mouth open, tongue mid-back, lips loosely rounded.
learnerTip: Round your lips loosely and push the tongue back slightly. Similar to /ɒ/ but longer and more rounded.
commonErrors: Merged with /ɑː/ in GA (cot-caught merger) — many American speakers don't distinguish these
Under-rounded by non-native speakers
dialectNote: In many American dialects, /ɔː/ and /ɑː/ have merged (cot-caught merger).
viNote: Gần "o" tiếng Việt kéo dài, môi tròn: law, saw, talk.

label: ER Sound
articulation: Open-mid central unrounded vowel. Tongue in mid-central position. In GA it is r-colored (retroflex).
learnerTip: In American English, curl the tip of your tongue back slightly while making this sound — it's an r-colored vowel.
commonErrors: Missing the r-color in GA — it should sound like 'er' not 'uh'
Adding too much r-color in RP, where /ɜː/ is non-rhotic
Confused with /ʌ/ — /ɜː/ is longer and often r-colored
dialectNote: In RP (British English) the final r is not pronounced — 'bird' sounds like /bɜːd/. In GA it is rhotic — /bɜːrd/.
viNote: Gần "ơ" kéo dài (bird, work). Giọng Mỹ có thêm âm r cong lưỡi ở cuối.

label: Long A
articulation: Starting position: mid front /e/. Glide upward to /ɪ/. The tongue rises and the jaw closes slightly.
learnerTip: Start with a relaxed /e/ sound then let your tongue glide up. Feel the two positions — don't stop in the middle.
commonErrors: Shortened to a pure /e/ without the glide (common in Spanish/Italian speakers)
Over-gliding so it sounds like 'ay-ee'
viNote: Gần "ây" (day gần "đây"). Phải lướt đủ sang /ɪ/, đừng đọc thành "e" đơn.

label: Long I
articulation: Starting position: open /a/ (or /ɑ/). Glide up to /ɪ/. Jaw closes, tongue rises.
learnerTip: Start with an open mouth /ah/, then close and raise your tongue toward /ee/. It's a big movement.
commonErrors: Starting too high — begin with a genuinely open mouth
Monophthongization: reduced to just /aː/ in some Southern American dialects
viNote: Gần "ai" tiếng Việt (my gần "mai"). Nhớ đọc rõ phụ âm cuối phía sau: time, nice.

label: OY Sound
articulation: Starting position: /ɔː/ (back rounded). Glide forward and up to /ɪ/. Lips start rounded then spread.
learnerTip: Start with rounded lips like /ɔː/, then glide your tongue forward and up. Feel the rounding release.
commonErrors: Under-rounding the start position
Not completing the glide to /ɪ/
viNote: Gần "oi" tiếng Việt (boy gần "bói"). Lướt nhanh từ "o" sang "i".

label: OW Sound
articulation: Starting position: open /a/. Glide back and up to /ʊ/. Lips start spread and become rounded.
learnerTip: Begin open and spread, then round your lips as the tongue moves back and up. Feel the lip movement.
commonErrors: Starting too far back like /ɔ/
Not completing the glide — the oo ending is important
viNote: Gần "ao" tiếng Việt (now gần "nao"), kết thúc bằng môi tròn.

label: Long O
articulation: Starting position: mid back /o/. Glide up and back to /ʊ/. Lips begin slightly rounded and increase.
learnerTip: Begin with rounded lips and let them tighten as the sound glides. Think 'oh-oo' in one smooth motion.
commonErrors: Realized as pure /oː/ without the glide (many European speakers)
Starting position too open like /ɑ/
viNote: Gần "âu" hoặc "ô" lướt sang "u" (go). Đừng đọc thành "ô" đơn. Giọng Anh-Anh là /əʊ/.

label: EAR Sound
articulation: Starting position: /ɪ/ (high front). Glide to /ə/ (center). Tongue relaxes and moves back.
learnerTip: Start with /ɪ/ and let your tongue relax down and back to schwa. It should flow naturally.
commonErrors: GA speakers often produce this as /ɪr/ (rhotic): 'near' = /nɪr/
Over-separating into two distinct vowels
dialectNote: In GA this is typically /ɪr/ (rhotic). /ɪə/ is an RP distinction.
viNote: Gần "ia" tiếng Việt (here gần "hia"), chủ yếu trong giọng Anh-Anh; giọng Mỹ đọc /ɪr/.

label: AIR Sound
articulation: Starting position: /e/ (mid front). Glide to /ə/. Tongue relaxes toward center.
learnerTip: Begin at /e/ then let everything relax. The movement is subtle — don't over-exaggerate.
commonErrors: GA speakers produce this as /ɛr/ — 'care' = /kɛr/
Confused with /eɪ/ by forgetting the schwa glide
dialectNote: In GA this merges with /ɛr/ (rhotic). /eə/ is primarily an RP distinction.
viNote: Gần "e" lướt sang "ơ" (hair, care), chủ yếu trong giọng Anh-Anh; giọng Mỹ đọc /ɛr/.

label: TH (Voiceless)
articulation: Voiceless dental fricative. Place the tip of your tongue lightly against or between your upper and lower teeth. Push air through — do NOT vibrate your vocal cords.
learnerTip: Stick your tongue tip slightly between your teeth and blow air. Feel that it is silent — no buzz from your throat.
commonErrors: Replaced with /s/ (common in Japanese, Spanish, Asian language speakers): 'think' → 'sink'
Replaced with /t/ (common in many L1s): 'think' → 'tink'
Voiced incorrectly as /ð/: 'thin' → 'then'
viNote: Tiếng Việt không có. Người Việt hay thay bằng "th" bật hơi, "t" hoặc "s". Đặt đầu lưỡi giữa hai hàm răng rồi thổi hơi, không rung dây thanh: think, three.

label: TH (Voiced)
spellingPatterns: th (function words and some content words)
articulation: Voiced dental fricative. Same tongue position as /θ/ but add vocal cord vibration — you should feel a buzz.
learnerTip: Same as /θ/ but hum while you do it. Place your fingers on your throat — you should feel vibration.
commonErrors: Replaced with /d/ (very common): 'the' → 'de'
Replaced with /z/ (common in European speakers): 'this' → 'zis'
Devoiced to /θ/: 'breathe' → 'breeth'
viNote: Tiếng Việt không có; hay bị đọc thành "đ", "d" hoặc /z/. Lưỡi giữa hai hàm răng và rung dây thanh: this, the, mother.

label: SH Sound
articulation: Voiceless postalveolar fricative. Tongue behind the alveolar ridge (not touching), lips slightly rounded. Air rushes through a wider opening than /s/.
learnerTip: Like /s/ but pull your tongue back slightly and round your lips. It's a hushing sound — 'shh!'
commonErrors: Confused with /s/ — /ʃ/ is further back and has lip rounding
Confused with /tʃ/ — /ʃ/ is continuous, no stop
viNote: Gần "s" cong lưỡi khi đọc chuẩn (như "sẽ") nhưng môi tròn và đưa ra trước: she, fish. Đừng đọc thành /s/: she khác see.

label: ZH Sound
articulation: Voiced postalveolar fricative. Same as /ʃ/ but with vocal cord vibration.
learnerTip: Say /ʃ/ then add voice from your throat. Feel the buzz. It sounds like the middle of 'measure'.
commonErrors: Devoiced to /ʃ/
Replaced with /dʒ/ by adding a stop at the start
viNote: Không có trong tiếng Việt. Là /ʃ/ có rung dây thanh: vision, measure. Người Việt hay thay bằng /z/ hoặc /ʃ/.

label: CH Sound
articulation: Voiceless postalveolar affricate. Start with the tongue against the ridge like /t/, then release into /ʃ/. It is one sound, not two.
learnerTip: Press your tongue to the ridge, build pressure, then release into a hush. 'ch' in 'cheese' is one quick motion.
commonErrors: Replaced with /ʃ/ alone (missing the stop onset)
Replaced with /ts/ (common in Japanese speakers)
viNote: Gần "ch" tiếng Việt nhưng môi tròn và bật hơi mạnh hơn: chair, watch. Ở cuối từ phải đọc rõ, không nuốt âm.

label: J Sound
articulation: Voiced postalveolar affricate. Same as /tʃ/ but with vocal cord vibration throughout.
learnerTip: Like /tʃ/ but add voice. Feel the buzz as you release. 'Jump' starts with the tongue on the ridge.
commonErrors: Devoiced to /tʃ/
Replaced with /y/ by some speakers (common in German L1): 'jump' → 'yump'
viNote: Không có trong tiếng Việt; hay bị đọc thành "gi" hoặc "ch". Là /tʃ/ có rung dây thanh: job, age, bridge.

label: NG Sound
articulation: Velar nasal. Tongue back presses against the soft palate (velum). Air flows through the nose. No lip or tongue-tip movement.
learnerTip: Say 'ng' like the end of 'sing' — feel the back of your tongue raised and touching the roof. No /g/ at the end in most GA words.
commonErrors: Adding a /g/ at the end: 'sing' → 'sing-g' (hypercorrection)
Replacing with /n/: 'sing' → 'sin'
Nasalizing the preceding vowel instead of producing a proper nasal stop
viNote: Giống "ng" tiếng Việt. Lưu ý đuôi -ing: không thêm /g/ và không đổi thành /n/: sing, thinking.

label: R Sound
articulation: Voiced alveolar approximant (GA). Curl the tongue tip back (retroflex) or bunch the tongue body up without touching the palate. Lips may be slightly rounded.
learnerTip: Never let your tongue touch anything for /ɹ/. Curl the tip back or pull the body up — it floats. This is the most uniquely American sound.
commonErrors: Replaced with a tap /ɾ/ (flap) by Spanish speakers: 'red' → 'ɾed'
Replaced with a trill /r/ by European speakers
Replaced with /l/ by some East Asian speakers: 'rice' → 'lice'
Over-rhotic: too much curl causing a 'pirate' sound
viNote: Khác "r" rung hay "r" giọng miền Nam. Rút hoặc cong lưỡi về sau, không chạm vòm miệng, môi hơi tròn: red, right. Người Việt hay nhầm với /z/ hoặc /l/.

label: L Sound
articulation: Voiced alveolar lateral approximant. Tongue tip touches the alveolar ridge (behind upper teeth). Air flows around the sides. In syllable-final position, it is 'dark' /ɫ/ — the tongue body raises at the back.
learnerTip: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. The tip stays up. For 'dark L' (final position), push the tongue body back as well.
commonErrors: Replaced with /r/ (especially by East Asian speakers): 'light' → 'right'
Missing the 'dark L' in final position: 'full' → 'fuh'
Vocalized dark L: 'full' → 'fouw'
viNote: Đầu từ giống "l" tiếng Việt. Cuối từ (feel, school) phải đưa đầu lưỡi chạm lợi trên; tiếng Việt không có "l" cuối nên người học hay bỏ mất âm này.

label: V Sound
articulation: Voiced labiodental fricative. Upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip. Air flows through creating friction, with vocal cord vibration.
learnerTip: Rest your upper teeth on your lower lip and push air through while humming. Feel the lip vibrating.
commonErrors: Replaced with /w/ (common in Japanese and some South Asian speakers): 'very' → 'wery'
Replaced with /b/ (common in Spanish speakers): 'van' → 'ban'
Devoiced to /f/: 'live' → 'life'
viNote: Răng trên chạm môi dưới và rung dây thanh: very, voice. Đừng thay bằng /w/, /b/ hoặc "d" kiểu giọng miền Nam.

label: W Sound
articulation: Voiced labial-velar approximant. Lips are tightly rounded and protruded, tongue is raised toward the velum. Then open into the following vowel.
learnerTip: Start with very rounded lips like /uː/, then quickly open into the next vowel. It is a glide — no friction.
commonErrors: Confused with /v/: not a fricative — no teeth involved
Under-rounded so it sounds like a plain vowel
viNote: Tròn môi rồi mở ra, gần âm đầu của "oa"/"uy" (we gần "uy"). Răng không chạm môi.
